title: Your Monthly Bills Just Got Easier: Understanding UPI Autopay
description: UPI Autopay lets you set up automatic payments for your regular expenses like bills and investments. It's like giving a digital standing instruction to your b.

faq.q: What kind of payments can I set up with UPI Autopay?
faq.a: You can set up UPI Autopay for a wide range of recurring payments, including mutual fund SIPs, loan EMIs, insurance premiums, utility bills (electricity, water, gas), mobile and DTH recharges, OTT subscriptions, and more.

faq.q: Is UPI Autopay safe to use?
faq.a: Yes, UPI Autopay is very safe. It operates within the secure framework of UPI, which is regulated by the RBI and NPCI. Your bank account details are not shared, and every mandate setup requires authentication using your UPI PIN.

faq.q: What happens if I don't have enough money in my account when a payment is due?
faq.a: If your account has insufficient funds, the UPI Autopay transaction will fail. You will receive a notification about the failed payment. Depending on the service provider, this might lead to late payment charges or disruption of the service.

faq.q: How do I check or manage my active UPI Autopay mandates?
faq.a: Most UPI apps have a dedicated section, often called "Mandates," "Autopay," or "Recurring Payments," where you can view all your active mandates. From there, you can see details, pause, modify, or cancel them.

faq.q: Can I set up UPI Autopay for an amount greater than ₹15,000?
faq.a: Currently, the maximum limit for UPI Autopay mandates for specific categories like mutual fund SIPs, insurance premiums, and loan EMIs is ₹15,000. For amounts above ₹5,000 within these categories, you will typically need to approve the transaction with your UPI PIN each time. For most other regular payments, the automatic deduction limit without additional approval is ₹5,000.
